priority.summary: Fermi Inc. discloses the immediate resignation of director Miles Everson, effective July 10, 2026, due to a disagreement over access to company books and records and the delegation of responsibility to the Finance Committee for overseeing financing transactions. Everson's resignation was submitted in a letter, which is attached to the filing as an exhibit, and he did not serve on any committee of the Board at the time of his resignation. The company believes Everson was granted full access to its books and records, except for materials related to pending litigation involving Toby Neugebauer, whom Everson represented on the Board.

Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment, after a Texas Business Court ordered the company to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players. The move is seen as a significant development in the ongoing governance dispute at Fermi, with Neugebauer arguing that the board's actions were an attempt to entrench itself and avoid scrutiny.
